newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama opens first money laundering trial.
newsitem.headline: Panama opens first money laundering trial.

text.p: Panama opened its first money laundering trial on Wednesday against five Lebanese entrepreneurs charged with laundering $3.5 million in drug money through the Atlantic coast free-trade zone, a Supreme Court spokeswoman said.
They are accused of changing foreign currency into U.S. dollars through front companies in the Colon free-trade zone located 50 miles (80 km) from Panama City, the spokeswoman said.
Panamanian and Canadian police opened an investigation into the ring on October 4, 1990 after checks from Colon businesses showed up in currency exchanges in Montreal.

Two of the men, Mohamad Noureddine Dahrouj and Walid Zayed, appeared in court on Wednesday in Colon. Also charged were Ahmad Noureddine Dahrouj and Samir Zayed who received provisional releases from prison earlier this year after being detained in Panama along with their brothers late last year.
One man, Hussein Handan, remains at large. The trial is expected to last four days. If found guilty, sentencing would come in 30 days.
